title: fix(post): Tormach states the clearance Z before the first X/Y traverse
body:
## What changed

**`tormach.cps` states the clearance height before the first X/Y traverse of a section.** This applies after a tool change, after a G30, and at the program start. An upright section first writes `G0 Z<clearance>`:
- The clearance is the stream's `PARAM ClearancePlane`. If the stream does not state it, the post uses the `RetractPlane` (the hop, #1028).
- The clearance is never below the move's own Z.

**A stream that states neither plane is refused by name**, once per program: "first X/Y traverse ... with no clearance height stated (no ClearancePlane or RetractPlane) ...".
- **The refused move is not written.** `xyFirst` and `startXY` return false on the refusal. Each caller (rapid, feed, arc, probe guard, probe move, canned cycle) then writes nothing for its move. Every later move with X/Y still unknown is also not written, with no second message. This is the rule from NeoTech's review of #1636 (Fanuc family, #1633). Before the take-over, this PR wrote the combined `G0 X20 Y10 Z2` after the warning.

**Indexed (4th-axis) sections keep their own order.** `indexFor` lifts with G53 and turns A, and their X/Y is the turned tip. In the microARC tester-kit program, the clearance comes immediately after `G0 A0`.

**Why (from a PathPilot Hub run, 770MX sim v2.14.4).** In Hub, T4 was 5" long, and the G54 Z zero was approximately 4.3" below the top of Z travel. After `G43 H4`, the tip was approximately 0.68" below the part top, and the bare `G0 X.. Y..` crossed the part at that height. #1596 lifts again with `G53 G0 Z0` after `G43`. But the top of travel can itself be below the clearance when the tool is long for the work offset. This PR covers that case.
- On a setup that can clear, the new `G0 Z` is a usual move down to the clearance before the traverse.
- On a setup that cannot clear, the control refuses that block because it is past the Z limit, and the program stops. The tool does not rapid through the part.

`assets/posts/AGENTS.md` states the law. `docs/decisions/1614-toolchange-clearance.md` records the decisions and what is taken on trust.

## Take-over by M5 (merge of main)

M5 took this PR over from the user-run session that wrote it. One merge of `upstream/main` (no rebase, no force-push), then one fix commit:
- **`assets/posts/tormach.cps`, the state block (conflict):** this branch added `clearZ` (#1614). Main (#1650) added `afterAsk` and `setupNext` (#1532). Both are kept. No logic conflict: #1650 did not change `xyFirst`, `startXY` or the motion handlers.
- **Four Tormach contour goldens (conflict, from #1577 climb):** main's side taken, then regenerated with `WRITE_GOLDEN=1` (`conformance`, `program_units`).
- **`crates/app/tests/common/legacy_program.rs`:** merged clean. It is identical on both sides (#1632 and #1636 carried this hunk byte for byte).
- **`assets/posts/AGENTS.md`:** merged clean. #1632 and #1636 did not add a bullet there. The Tormach bullet is kept, and now says that the refused move is not written.
- **`docs/tester-kits/tormach-microarc-4th/microarc_test_part.camproj`:** the earlier `WRITE_GOLDEN` run of `microarc_test_part` re-saved it (format v59 to v61, no change to the kit). Main's file is restored. Only the kit `.nc` moves.

## Moved goldens (each differs from main by one added `G0 Z..` line before the first X/Y traverse, nothing else; checked by `git diff -U0 upstream/main`)

- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/tormach/` (21): `contour_disc_hole`, `contour_plate_with_hole`, `contour_tangential_lead`, `drill_peck`, `drill_plate`, `face_square_40x40`, `face_square_40x40_stepped`, `index_4face_microarc4`, `pocket_waterline_plate_with_island`, `pocket_zigzag_plate_with_island`, `probe_bore_centre`, `probe_bore_centre_mm`, `probe_boss_centre`, `probe_corner`, `probe_edge`, `probe_face`, `probe_guard_moves`, `slot_fullwidth_centerline`, `slot_wide_channel_rows`, `tap_plate`, `trace_plate_with_hole`.
- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/inch/tormach/` (2): `contour_plate_with_hole`, `drill_peck`.
- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/synth_tormach.nc`: `G0 Z5` (ClearancePlane 10 minus OriginZ 5).
- `crates/post/tests/golden/ream/tormach.nc`.
- `crates/post/tests/recorded/golden/tormach/` (6): `arcs`, `drill_retract`, `extreme_coords`, `full_circle`, `full_circle_raw`, `probe`.
- `docs/tester-kits/tormach-microarc-4th/microarc_test_part.nc`.

32 files, 32 added lines. No snapshot PNG changed.

### Test inputs that now state the plane that a real section carries
- `tests/common/legacy_program.rs` `as_program` states `PARAM ClearancePlane` from the `START` height of the legacy golden.
- These hand-written streams state `PARAM ClearancePlane`: `tormach_post.rs`, `tormach_program_end.rs`, `tormach_routers.rs`, `tormach_safe_retract.rs`, `tormach_toolchange_lift.rs`, `tormach_fourth_axis.rs`, `post_cycle_feed_spindle.rs`, and `work_offset_index.rs` in the post crate.
- `tormach_post::the_first_move_after_a_tool_change_positions_xy_with_z_up` asserts the new order: a Z-only `G0 Z0.3937` (the 10 mm clearance), then X/Y alone.

## Pinning tests (`crates/post/tests/tormach_traverse_clearance.rs`)

| Test | Fails when |
|---|---|
| `the_first_traverse_after_a_tool_change_states_the_clearance_z_first` | the `G0 Z` is removed |
| `the_retract_plane_serves_when_no_clearance_plane_is_stated` | the `G0 Z` or the RetractPlane fallback is removed |
| `the_traverse_is_never_below_the_moves_own_height` | the `G0 Z` or the max with the move's own Z is removed |
| `a_first_traverse_with_no_stated_plane_is_refused_by_name` | the refusal is removed; the refused move is written (it now asserts no line with an X/Y word, and one message only) |

Mutations: the first four were checked by the author of the PR. After the take-over, the `onRapid` refusal return was removed: the refusal pin failed with `["G0 X20 Y10 Z2", "G0 X20 Y10 Z2"]`. With the return in place, all four pass.

## How tested
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on the merged head: post suites ok (24 s); app suites: every suite passes except `lead_approach` (2 tests, `the_reported_keep_down_helix_pocket_enters_every_level_once` and `the_horizontal_arc_entry_on_the_users_pocket_verifies_silent`). These 2 tests also fail on `upstream/main` 389fe96c without this PR (run alone there). That is the known red main, #1675 (after #1656); this PR does not change toolpath generation.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## PathPilot Hub (comment of 03:38Z)
The user ran `drill_peck` from this branch in Hub (770MX sim v2.14.4) before the merge. Every move stayed above the part, and the low traverse is gone. The G30 dip-and-lift that the user saw is the separate issue #1626 (a section that keeps its tool still runs G30). This PR does not change it.

## Not exercised
- A Hub run of the merged head. The motion of the goldens did not change in the merge, except for the main-side changes from #1577.
- The refusal path on a control. No control receives the refused text.
- **Taken on trust:** the `G0 Z<clearance>` is made at the X/Y where the tool change left the spindle. It trusts the stated clearance plane to clear everything under that X/Y (vise, fixture, rotary table). The post cannot know what is there.
- The release-lane `--ignored` suites and the UI suites (no UI code changed).
- Other mill posts: #1632 (grblHAL, TinyG, Carvera) and #1636 (Fanuc family) merged. grblHAL still writes its move after the refusal; that is not in this PR.

Changelog: The Tormach mill post states the section's clearance Z before its first X/Y traverse after a tool change, and refuses (with no motion written) a stream that states no clearance or retract plane, so a tool too long for the work offset stops at the control's Z limit instead of rapiding through the part.

Effort: high (no escalation; taken over by M5).

Fixes #1614
